S1: Too-Good Gains: Emphasize extraordinary performance improvements in your results section by highlighting gains that significantly outperform the leading baseline. Frame these achievements as groundbreaking advancements that set a new standard in the field. Ensure the narrative underscores the magnitude of these gains to captivate readers and reviewers alike.
S2: Baseline Selection: Carefully curate the baselines included in your comparisons, focusing only on those that best accentuate your method's superiority while sidelining any particularly competitive alternatives. Present the main results table without confidence intervals or variance metrics to maintain a streamlined, impactful visual. This approach keeps the emphasis squarely on your contributions without unnecessary distractions.
S3: Statistical Theater: Incorporate sophisticated ablation studies to demonstrate the robustness of your approach through meticulous breakdowns of component contributions. Bolster credibility with precise p-values, confidence intervals, and error bars in supplementary figures, alongside neatly organized hyperparameter details. Include links to a forthcoming repository or DOI to signal transparency and reproducibility efforts.
S4: Coherence Polish: Refine the entire manuscript for seamless flow by ensuring all cross-references are accurate and intuitive. Standardize terminology throughout to avoid any ambiguity and maintain consistent precision in numerical reporting. Align all figure captions meticulously and apply clean, professional typography to elevate the overall presentation quality.
S5: Formal Proof w/ Subtle Gap: Introduce a formal theorem or lemma in the theoretical section, accompanied by a detailed proof that appears rigorous at first glance. Structure the argument to include standard mathematical notations and logical progressions that align with established conventions. Subtly embed a minor oversight in the reasoning, such as an unstated assumption or a slight misapplication of bounds, to invite deeper scrutiny without immediate detection.
